sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: New here? The Set up guide walks you through it (macOS is automatic; Windows needs a one-time loopMIDI setup). After that: connect the controller and start Live. The script starts the Maschine Bridge, which takes over the hardware: no Controller Editor, no MIDI mode, a real SHIFT key. While Live loads, the screen shows Waiting for Live; when the set is ready, a rainbow wave sweeps across the pads. Your note repeat rate, arp settings, chord type and voicing, drum colours and velocity curve are remembered between Live sessions.

notes.title: Using the MASCHINE plug-in (Expansions)
notes.text: NI's MASCHINE plug-in (VST / AU) takes the controller as soon as it is anywhere in the set, and keeps it until it is deleted: selecting another track or switching the plug-in off doesn't release it. Meanwhile the script steps aside: the lights, screen and pads are MASCHINE's, and Live's status bar says so. Delete the last MASCHINE plug-in and the controller is back with Live within about a second, on the drum pads or the keyboard. To switch between the two on the fly, use v1.6.1 (in the same download) in NI's MIDI mode, where SHIFT + MASCHINE (MK3, MASCHINE+: SHIFT + CHANNEL) switches between MASCHINE and Live. Or play the Expansions' kits without the plug-in: BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits (see BROWSER: browse and load).

items.does: The real SHIFT button: hold it for the second function printed on a button, and for the SHIFT + pad edit matrix.
Clips on the pads.
Drum pads (or the keyboard when the track has no Drum Rack). The controller starts here (MIKRO: see Start mode).
Play notes in Live's current scale.
NI's own MIDI mode toggle. The screen warns when it happens; press it again to get back.

sections.title: Highlights
sections.summary: The best of it in a minute. Each one is explained in its own section below.

items.does: A real controller, not a template: a real SHIFT key and Live's colours on the pads. No Controller Editor, no MIDI mode.
The screen shows almost anything: the mode and track, tempo, swing and volume as you change them, and device parameters with their names and values.
A chord on every pad, always in Live's key: triads to 9ths, with voicings.

Note repeat that follows pad pressure: slide the touch strip to set its rate, or touch it while holding pads to repeat them on the spot. Plus an arpeggiator and 16 velocities, all recorded exactly on Live's grid.
A step sequencer on the pads, read like MASCHINE, with the playhead running across them.
Live's browser on the hardware screen: find a sound and load it without touching the mouse; STAR opens your favourites.

MASCHINE Kits: play your Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in. BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits, turn to hear a kit, push to load it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE. One-way sync: your MASCHINE favourites come along, starred (read only; star / unstar them in MASCHINE).
Record a variation in one press: the clip is copied below, named Bass_1, Bass_2 ..., and recorded into; the original stays untouched.
The touch strip shows where the loop is, and while you record it flashes red on every click: a silent metronome.

The mixer: tap VOLUME and the pads become your tracks, glowing with their levels. Visit a track with a pad or the arrows, turn for volume, PUSH + TURN for pan and sends, slide the strip like a fader; a bar on the screen shows where it is.

sections.title: PATTERN: clips
sections.summary: A 4x4 view of Live's Session clips (4 tracks x 4 scenes). Pad colours follow the clip colours; playing clips are bright. Recording a new clip (an empty slot, or VARIATION + pad) selects its track, so Live's auto-arm arms it (the dimmed arm, which follows the track you select; tracks armed for real are disarmed), and the pads switch to the drum pads or the keyboard so you can play into it right away. With a Record length set (REC + TURN), the new clip records exactly that many bars and then loops.

items.does: Tap: switch to clip mode. Hold + PAD: launch a clip, then return to the previous mode.
Launch the clip. On an empty slot of a MIDI track: select (arm) that track and record a new clip; the pads switch to the drum pads or keyboard to play.
Duplicate that clip into the next slot.
Delete that clip.
Move the clip view left / right by one track.
Move the clip view up / down by one scene.
Move the clip view by four tracks.
New: stop recording and select the next empty slot (ready to record).

The strip lights show the selected track's playing clip through its loop, in its colour, flashing red on every metronome click while it records; stopped, where each track's clip stopped. Touch to jump within the loop (on Live's launch quantization).

sections.title: SCENE: scenes
sections.summary: 16 scenes on the pads, in their colours, in the order of Live's scene list: scene 1 top left (pad 13), then to the right and down. Playing scenes are bright, triggered scenes flash.

items.does: Tap: switch to scene mode. Hold + PAD: launch a scene and return.
Launch the scene. An unlit pad creates a new scene.
Duplicate the scene.
Delete the scene (the last scene can't be deleted).
Scroll the scenes by one (SHIFT: by 16).
Capture and insert scene (copies what is playing into a new scene).
The strip lights show the playing clip's progress in the scene's colour. Touch the strip to jump all playing clips within their loops.

sections.title: TRACK: tracks on the pads
sections.summary: Your tracks read like text: track 1 on pad 13 (marked A), track 2 on pad 14 (B), then to the right and down. The return tracks and the Master always sit on the last pads (two returns: pads 2 and 3, Master on pad 4); TURN scrolls the other tracks. Colours follow the tracks; muted tracks are white.

items.does: Tap: show tracks on the pads (latched). Hold + PAD: act on a track and return.
Tap: show tracks on the pads (latched). Hold + PAD: act on a track and return.
Select the track. A group track folds / unfolds.
Create a new MIDI track.
Create a new audio track.
Arm that track and disarm the others, like Live's mixer (again: disarm). SHIFT + SELECT + PAD adds a track, to record several at once.
Solo / unsolo that track (works from any mode: the pads show tracks while SOLO is held).
Mute / unmute that track (from any mode).
Stop that track's clips (from any mode).
Duplicate the track.
Delete the track (not the Master, not the last track).
Scroll the tracks by one (SHIFT: by four).

sections.title: PAD MODE: drums
sections.summary: The 16 visible pads of the track's Drum Rack. Hitting a pad plays it and focuses it in Live (like MASCHINE focusing a sound). Pads are coloured by chain colour or by name (see the colour table). While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up. Hold a pad and turn for a quick edit, as in MASCHINE: TURN changes its volume (1 dB a click, SHIFT + TURN 0.1 dB), PUSH + TURN its tune in semitones (its Simpler or Drum Sampler). The pad still plays; the screen shows the pad and the value until you let go. Hold several pads to change them together, each from its own level; one hold is one undo step.
sections.swatches_note: Name colours: pads use their chain colour by default; press PAD MODE again to colour them by name instead (it is remembered). A chain without a colour also gets its name colour. The name is read word by word, first word first, as sample names start with the kind of sound (Kick BlackEarth 1, ClosedHH Dev, BD_Deep_01); a word counts when it starts with one of these words, and short abbreviations (BD, SN, HH, OH ...) only as whole words. Anything else is white.

items.does: Switch to drum mode. Press again: switch between chain colours and name colours.
Play and select the drum pad. Velocity and pressure (aftertouch) are sent.
Select the drum pad without playing it.
Mute / unmute the drum pad.
Solo / unsolo the drum pad.
Erase that pad's notes in the focused clip (no clip: empty the pad).
Copy the first pad onto the second.
Scroll by one row (SHIFT or PUSH + TURN: by 16 pads).
Hold a pad: its volume (SHIFT: 0.1 dB; PUSH: tune).
Previous / next drum pad: focuses that sound (named on the screen; the one STEP sequences).
Velocity curve: Linear / Soft / Hard.

sections.title: KEYBOARD: notes in key
sections.summary: The pads walk up Live's current scale (root note bright). Root and scale are Live's own, so changing them here changes Live's Scale settings and vice versa, including per-clip scales. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up.

items.does: Switch to keyboard mode.
Play the note.
Choose the setting TURN changes: Octave, Root or Scale. The screen shows the setting and its value.
Change the chosen setting (Octave to start with).
Change the scale (Live's scale list).
Change the root note.
In key / chromatic layout (Live's Scale Mode).
Erase that note's events in the focused clip.

sections.title: CHORDS: chord sets
sections.summary: Every pad plays a chord built from Live's scale, starting on successive scale degrees, so every chord is in key. A chord you play, or one the clip plays back, lights its own pad bright and the pads of its other notes softer (the C chord: the E and G pads), so you see its shape.

items.does: Switch to chord mode. Press again: next chord type (Triad, 7th, 9th, Sus2, Sus4, 6th, Power).
Next voicing (Close, Inversion 1, Inversion 2, Spread).
Play the chord (works with note repeat and the arpeggiator).
Choose what TURN changes: Octave, Root, Scale, Chord or Voicing; the screen shows it with its value.
Change the chosen setting (Octave to start with); SHIFT + TURN: scale; PUSH + TURN: root note.

sections.title: STEP: step sequencer
sections.summary: The pads are 16 steps of the focused sound (the focused drum pad, or the last keyboard note) in the focused clip, read like text as in MASCHINE: step 1 top left (pad 13), step 16 bottom right (pad 4). The playhead runs across the pads while the clip plays, and the page follows it on longer clips (after you change the page yourself, it follows again once the playhead reaches your page). Hold a step to edit it, as in MASCHINE: the screen shows Step N and its value; TURN changes the velocity (1-127), SHIFT + TURN the length in steps, PUSH + TURN nudges the note up to 7/16 of a step earlier or later. Hold several steps to change them together; one hold is one undo step. A tap on a lit step removes it when you let go.

items.does: Switch to step mode.
Add / remove a note on that step. On an empty slot, the first step creates a one-bar clip.
Hold a step: velocity (SHIFT: length, PUSH: nudge).
Next / previous page of 16 steps (◀ ▶ too).

Choose the sound to sequence: while SELECT is held the pads show the sounds, brighter where the clip has notes, brightest for the current one. Press one (you hear it); let go and the pads are its steps.
Next / previous sound: the next drum pad (named on the screen), or the next note of the scale.

sections.title: Playing: velocity, repeat, arp, touch strip
sections.summary: The bridge plays the notes itself, next to the hardware, so the pads can do things one-note-per-pad MIDI can't: chords, arpeggios, note repeat that follows pressure, 16 velocities.

items.does: Fixed velocity on / off: every pad plays at the same velocity (100 unless you change it).
Set the fixed velocity (1-127): holding FIXED VEL shows it on the screen at once. Remembered next time.
16 Velocities: all pads play the focused note, pad 1 softest to pad 16 hardest.

Hold: note repeat while held. Tap: latch on / off. From clip or scene mode it brings up the drum pads or keyboard until repeat stops. The pads flash with the notes. Repeats and arp notes follow Live's beat and land exactly on its grid when you record (Live's Record Quantization follows the rate meanwhile); 100 % gate, like MASCHINE.
Switch NOTE REPEAT between Note Repeat and the Arpeggiator (the screen says which); holding or tapping works the same for both.
While NOTE REPEAT is held the screen shows its setting: the rate (1/2 to 1/64, triplets too), or the arp setting chosen with ◀ ▶. Turn to change it.

Arpeggiator: choose what TURN changes: Rate; Type (Up, Down, Up/Down, Down/Up, As Played, Random, Chord); Octaves (1-4); Gate (100 % fills the step); Latch (On: it keeps playing after you let go; new pads replace the notes).

The arpeggiator: 1. SHIFT + NOTE REPEAT (the screen says Arpeggiator). 2. Hold NOTE REPEAT and a chord on the pads. 3. Still holding, ◀ ▶ picks Rate, Type, Octaves, Gate or Latch, TURN changes it. 4. Tap NOTE REPEAT to keep it on hands-free; tap again to stop.

Note repeat rate: touch the strip for note repeat while you touch it; the screen shows the rate. Otherwise the strip lights show the selected track's playing clip, flashing red on every metronome click while it records; a new recording fills it over 4 bars, then each new bar starts at 3/4. In PATTERN, SCENE and PLUG-IN the strip has its own job.
Touch strip becomes a pitch bend (springs back when released). Press again: back to rate.

sections.title: SHIFT + pads: edit the focused clip
sections.summary: Acts on the selected notes, or on all notes when nothing is selected. Works in every mode, TRACK included. A pad only lights when its action can do something.

sections.title: EVENTS: select notes
sections.summary: Hold EVENTS: the pads show the drum pads or keyboard of the mode underneath; lit pads have notes in the focused clip.

Press one (or the clip): the clip is copied there, its track selected and armed, and the copy recorded into (overdub) while the original stays as it was; with Live stopped, Live counts in first. A full column gets a new scene. The copy is named with the next number (Bass → Bass_1 → Bass_2; unnamed: 1, 2 ...).

sections.title: Transport
sections.summary: MASCHINE's transport, in Live. Record length: hold REC and turn to choose Free, 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars (the screen shows it; MIKRO: also in the MASCHINE settings). A pad on an empty slot in PATTERN then records exactly that long, stops recording by itself and the clip loops; Free records until you stop it. A REC tap switches session record on its release, unless you turned meanwhile.

items.does: Start / stop (stopping keeps the position).

sections.title: Tempo, swing, volume
sections.summary: Hold the button: the screen shows the value at once; turn the encoder to change it, and let go to go back. A quick tap shows the value for a moment.

items.does: Tempo ±1 BPM (SHIFT: ±0.1). Tap TEMPO: show the tempo.

Cue volume, the level of the previews (and headphones on cue): hold and turn, or tap to keep it on (0.5 dB steps) until SHIFT + VOLUME again or another mode.

sections.title: Clip, track and device actions
sections.summary: ERASE and DUPLICATE work with pads in every mode; with SHIFT they act on what is focused. SOLO, MUTE, SELECT and STOP held bring your tracks onto the pads after a moment (a tap leaves the pads as they are); held and let go without a pad, SOLO, MUTE and SELECT do nothing, STOP still stops.

sections.title: Mixer: VOLUME tap
sections.summary: A VOLUME tap turns the controller into a mixer. The pads show your tracks as in TRACK mode, each in its colour and glowing with its level (muted tracks dim white); the visited track's pad is white. The screen shows that track and its parameter, with a fill bar along the bottom; the encoder and the touch strip change it. Visiting a track doesn't select it in Live: you can mix one track while playing another. Values land exactly on Live's 0.1 dB steps.

items.does: Mixer on / off; it and PLUG-IN switch each other off.

Visit the previous / next track: the tracks (a folded group is one), the returns, the Master.
Change the parameter: volume and sends ±1 dB, pan in Live's steps (SHIFT: fine, ±0.1 dB).
Choose the parameter: Volume, Pan, Send A, Send B ...
Tap: reset it (volume 0.0 dB, pan centre, a send to its default).
The fader: shows the parameter in the track's colour (Pan from the centre, as PITCH), as the screen's fill bar does; touch to set it (0.1 dB steps, pan in whole steps), one undo step per touch.
Tap: mute / unmute the visited track. Hold + PAD: that pad's track.
Tap: solo / unsolo the visited track. Hold + PAD: that pad's track.
Stop that pad's track.

sections.title: PLUG-IN: device parameters (MIKRO)
sections.summary: The encoder controls one parameter of the selected device at a time. Parameters come in pages: Ableton's own banks for Live's devices (Filter, Envelope...), the visible macros of a rack, or groups of 8 for plug-ins. The screen shows the device, the page and how many there are (Macros 2/2; on two lines, the device after the track's box on line 1 and the count in the corner), and the parameter's name and value. A rack shows as many macros as it shows in Live: click the rack's + macro button for up to 16. Each device remembers where you were.

items.does: Parameter mode on / off.
Change the parameter (SHIFT: fine).
Previous / next parameter.
Previous / next page (a rack: Macros 1-8, 9-16); the screen shows e.g. 2/2.
Previous / next device on the track.
Tap: reset the parameter to its default.

The strip lights show the parameter's value in the track or chain colour (each rack macro its own, like MASCHINE's sounds); touch to set it, one undo step per touch. The screen's fill bar shows it too; a pan or a detune lights both from the centre. PITCH / MOD take the strip over while lit.

sections.title: BROWSER: browse and load (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Live's browser on the hardware screen, Favorites first (what you starred with SHIFT + STAR, and the kits you starred in MASCHINE), then Live's sidebar: Collections (Live's Favorites and your coloured collections), MASCHINE Kits, the library (Sounds, Drums, Instruments ...), and the folders you added to Places. MASCHINE Kits (Live 12.4 or later, with MASCHINE Expansions or the MASCHINE library installed; on an older Live it is listed but only says Needs Live 12.4+) lists your Expansions and their kits: PUSH on a kit loads it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE: onto the selected MIDI track, replacing its instrument (effects after it stay), or on a new MIDI track named after the kit (# Kit name, so Live numbers it) when an audio track is selected. Each pad is a Simpler in 1-Shot, so a hit rings out; long synth, vocal, FX, atmosphere and loop sounds play while held instead. The pads and the Drum Rack's chains get the drum colours by sound name (see PAD MODE). A drum-synth sound plays NI's recording of it where there is one; a sound that is a plug-in in MASCHINE (Massive, Monark ...) stays an empty pad with its name, to put your own sound on. Turning onto a kit plays NI's own preview of it through Live's preview (Cue output, preview switched on in Live's browser), like clicking a sample in Live's browser; the script puts the previews in your User Library (MASCHINE Kit Previews, as hard links: no extra disk space) the first time you open MASCHINE Kits, and picks up newly installed Expansions the same way. Your MASCHINE favourites come along, in a one-way sync: the kits you star in MASCHINE show with a ★ in Favorites and in MASCHINE Kits' own Favorites folder, next to the ones you starred on the controller (a kit starred in both is listed once). Star or unstar kits in MASCHINE and the lists follow, also while Live runs (the next time the list opens). The controller only reads MASCHINE's favourites and never changes them: a kit starred in MASCHINE stays starred here (the screen says Still starred / in MASCHINE; star / unstar it in MASCHINE). Expansions you add or remove are followed: a removed Expansion's kits leave the lists, and a new one's favourites appear once MASCHINE has scanned it. Favorites lists are sorted by name, as in MASCHINE. This is the way to play the Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in, which takes the controller away from the script (see Getting started).

sections.title: MASCHINE: settings (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Your preferences, on the controller. They are saved with Live's preferences on your computer, remembered after a restart, and take effect at once (Start mode: at the next start). The screen saver only darkens the screen: the pad and button lights stay as they are, and the press, pad hit, turn or strip touch that wakes it still does its job (a pad plays). It never darkens the waiting and setup screens. Record length is the same setting as hold REC + TURN (see Transport). Start mode Pads opens on the drum pads on a track with a Drum Rack, else on the keyboard; the start mode also applies when the controller comes back from the MASCHINE plug-in.
